question: How many cumulative confirmed New World screwworm animal cases in the US will APHIS report as of October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Cumulative count is monotonic and stood at 50 on 2026-09-21 (48 TX, 2 NM), so this is purely about additions over 10 days. Reference class: 10-day increments in this same series during the post-peak regime (Aug 1 - Sep 21) - 47 on Aug 26, 49 on Sep 15, 50 on Sep 21, i.e. ~1.15-1.4 per 10 days, versus ~4.5 per 10 days over the full outbreak (June 30 cases, July 13, August 4 per NOTUS). Status quo is continued deceleration: TAHC lists rolling infested-zone releases across 13+ counties since late August, sterile-fly releases at scale, and all cases still in domestic animals with no wildlife or feral detections. Counter-evidence both ways: APHIS staff and TX Ag Commissioner Miller publicly doubt the decline (possible under-reporting that could correct upward in a batch), and Sept cases in Presidio Co. TX and Grant Co. NM show seeding into new geographies; against that, fall detection effort in wildlife mostly starts after Oct 1 (TX archery season opens ~Oct 3). I center on ~1-2 additions (median 51), keep 50 credible (~27%) since the last confirmed case was Sep 17 and gaps of a week-plus are common in this regime, and price a thin right tail for a premises-level cluster or surveillance backlog. No matching human market exists; the Manifold wild-animal contract differs on event, deadline and resolution source, so I did not blend it.

calls.dossier:
US NWS ANIMAL-CASE COUNT - RESEARCH DIGEST (compiled 2026-09-21)

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: Resolves off the cumulative confirmed US ANIMAL-case figure on the APHIS 'Confirmed Detections of New World Screwworm' dashboard in effect 2026-10-01 ET (most recent figure published on or before that date if not updated that day). NOT fly-trap/wild-fly detections, NOT human cases, NOT Mexico/Central America totals. Trackers (genomicepi 'Animal cases', dvm360 'Total confirmed animal cases') restate the same APHIS data; APHIS governs on conflict. Count is cumulative and monotonic - it can only rise. dvm360 states the dashboard updates daily at 6 p.m. ET; dvm360's own tracker refreshes Fridays. The APHIS landing page carries a 'Last Modified: August 21, 2026' stamp while the embedded dashboard updates separately.

EVENT WINDOW: Cumulative accrual runs 2026-06-03 (first US case) -> 2026-10-01 per the criteria; as of Now (2026-09-21T22:10Z), 110 of 120 days = ~92% elapsed. Only the 2026-09-21 -> 2026-10-01 tail remains open.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: the count remains at its 2026-09-21 level plus whatever the recent per-week confirmation rate adds over 10 days.

EVIDENCE
- 2026-09-21 (Houston Public Media tracker, restating APHIS): 50 cumulative US infestations confirmed since the outbreak began - 48 Texas, 2 New Mexico.
- 2026-09-17: second New Mexico case confirmed, a horse in Grant County (first NM case was a dog, Lea County).
- 2026-09-09: first US equine case in ~60 years, a working ranch horse in Presidio County, TX (Big Bend region); a fourth infected dog reported the same week (dvm360).
- 2026-09-15 (dvm360 tracker): USDA count stood at 49.
- 2026-08-26: 47 cumulative.
- 2026-07-09 (American Farm Bureau): 33 cumulative (32 TX, 1 NM), ALL in domestic animals; zero wildlife and zero feral-animal cases as of that date. No wildlife/feral case has been reported since, through 2026-09-21.
- 2026-06-03: first case, 3-week-old beef calf, La Pryor, Zavala County, TX, ~50 miles from the Mexico border.
- Texas Animal Health Commission (accessed 2026-09-21): 17 Texas counties with cases; 39 Texas premises with cases. Multiple counties released from infested-zone status since late August 2026 - Gillespie, Kerr, Kimble, La Salle, Webb, Coke, Tom Green, Uvalde, Zavala, Bandera, Medina, Jim Hogg, Starr.
- NOTUS/Washington Sun ('Screwworm Cases Are Going Down. Experts Are Suspicious.'): USDA attributes the decline to a five-prong strategy incl. ~1 billion sterile males released. Counter-signals in the same piece: a former USDA manager says the decline 'doesn't make a lot of sense, biologically'; TX Ag Commissioner Sid Miller's team caught suspected screwworm in traps that USDA labs returned negative; current APHIS employees call the absence of trapped wild flies 'suspicious'; ranchers may avoid self-reporting because quarantine carries no indemnification (USDA provided indemnity for bird flu, not screwworm).
- USDA has launched NWS resources for wildlife professionals and hunters (dvm360). Texas general deer season opens in November and archery ~Oct 3 - i.e. the hunter-surveillance channel largely opens AFTER 2026-10-01.
- Regional context (PLoS NTDs narrative review, 2026-09-21): >209,400 animal cases and >2,500 human cases cumulatively across Mexico/Central America as of Aug 2026; detections in 30 of Mexico's 32 states. Mexico human cases: 692 across 27 states as of 2026-09-18, 11 new in the prior week (El Universal). These are separate instruments and do not feed the US animal count.
- Texas Standard, 2026-09-18: livestock illegally moved across remote stretches of the US-Mexico border identified as an ongoing introduction pathway.

BASE RATES (US animal-case additions)
- Unconditional, over the whole outbreak 2026-06-03 to 2026-09-21: 49 additions / 110 days = ~4.5 per 10-day window.
- Conditional on the early exponential phase (June): 30 cases in June alone (NOTUS) = ~10 per 10-day window; the Jun 21 -> Jul 1 window alone added ~17.
- Conditional on the post-peak regime (July onward, NOTUS monthly counts): July ~13 cases = ~4.2 per 10 days; August 4 cases = ~1.3 per 10 days.
- Conditional on the most recent month (Aug 26 -> Sep 21, APHIS/dvm360/HPM): 3 additions in 26 days = ~1.15 per 10 days. Within it: Aug 26 -> Sep 15 = +2 over 20 days; Sep 15 -> Sep 21 = +1 over 6 days.
- Observed spread of 10-day increments in the last ~8 weeks of this series: 1 to 2, no window above 3. Over the last 16 weeks: 1 to 17.
- Species composition to date: cattle, sheep, goats, dogs (4), horses (2). 100% domestic.

MARKETS: Searched Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold and bookmakers for a contract on the US NWS case count. None found that matches this question's threshold/deadline/resolution source. The one screwworm contract located is a Manifold market on whether a WILD animal will be infected in the US before 2027 - different event, different deadline (2026-12-31), no count threshold, thin volume (~1.7k).

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: the raw APHIS dashboard row-level detection table (the page renders an embedded dashboard that does not appear in fetched text; direct fetch of genomicepi.com and dvm360 returned HTTP 403); any confirmation dated between 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-21; any APHIS statement forecasting the expected case count for October; any published per-week APHIS case-increment time series; any announcement of a change to APHIS's counting methodology or dashboard cadence.
calls.reference_class: Ten-day increments in the cumulative confirmed US NWS animal-case count during the Aug 1 - Sep 21, 2026 post-peak/containment regime (observed increments of 1-2 per 10-day window, mean ~1.3), contrasted with the unconditional full-outbreak rate of ~4.5 per 10 days since June 3, 2026

calls.reasoning: Count is monotonic and stands at 50 as of 2026-09-21 (48 TX, 2 NM), so the question is purely how many confirmations post in ~9.7 days. Reference class: 10-day windows of this outbreak since Aug 1 2026, which have averaged ~1.1-1.3 new cases (August total 3-4; 47 on Aug 26 -> 48 on Sep 5 -> 50 on Sep 17-21). A Poisson/neg-binomial with mean ~1.2 over the remaining window puts ~33% on no change (50), ~29% on 51, and ~80% at or below 52. Downward pressure: officials report northward spread slowed, TAHC lifting infested-zone status in Gillespie/Kerr/Kimble/La Salle/Webb, sterile-fly capacity up. Upward pressure: NOTUS reporting that experts consider the decline suspicious (no indemnity = rancher reporting disincentive), the Sept border reopening to Mexican livestock, and herd-level clusters that can add several cases at once. Dashboard lag trims the effective detection window to ~Sep 28. Escape above 58.5 requires 9+ confirmations in 10 days - only a backlog dump or a new focus does that, priced at 2%. No market matches this contract (see reasoning above on Kalshi/Manifold). Main caveat: I could not read the APHIS dashboard directly (Power BI embed; genomicepi 403), so the starting level rests on multiple concordant news restatements rather than the primary instrument.

- 2026-09-05 (Wikipedia, '2026 United States New World Screwworm outbreak'): 48 known US cases; species to date cattle, sheep, goats, dogs, horses - all domestic.
- 2026-08-26: 47 cumulative cases (question background, sourced to APHIS).
- Early Sept 2026 (NOTUS/Washington Sun): only 4 cases detected in the whole of August, none in cattle; June had ~30.
- 2026-07-03: 32 known cases.
- 2026-08-31 (TAHC news release) and 2026-09-21 reporting: Texas lifting infested-zone designations in parts of Gillespie, Kerr, Kimble, La Salle and Webb counties after months of surveillance; federal officials say northward spread has slowed.
- TAHC page (undated snapshot): 17 Texas counties affected, 39 Texas premises with cases - premises count is lower than the animal-case count, i.e. some premises contributed multiple animals.
- NOTUS/Washington Sun: multiple current and former USDA officials and TX Ag Commissioner Sid Miller call the decline biologically implausible; zero wildlife cases and zero confirmed wild-fly-trap positives despite suspect trap catches; ranchers face quarantine with no USDA indemnity (unlike avian influenza), a documented disincentive to report.
- 2026-09-21 (PLoS NTD review, Frias et al.): >209,400 animal cases and >2,500 human cases cumulatively across the Americas as of Aug 2026; detections in 30 of Mexico's 32 states; sterile-fly production capacity being built in Texas and Chiapas.
- 2026-09-18 (El Universal): Mexico at 692 confirmed human cases across 27 states, 11 new in the prior week - the regional reservoir remains active.
- USDA has launched NWS resources for hunters and wildlife professionals (dvm360), and relies partly on AI-assisted wildlife camera review that Miller publicly criticized as too low-resolution to spot wounds.

BASE RATES (new APHIS-confirmed US animal cases per 10-day window):
- Over the full outbreak, 2026-06-03 to 2026-09-21 (~11 windows): mean ~4.5/window, but bimodal - June windows ran roughly 7-9 each, post-July windows roughly 0-2 each.
- Conditional on the post-peak regime, 2026-08-01 to 2026-09-21 (~5 windows): ~1.1-1.3 per window; August total 3-4 for the month; Aug 26 -> Sep 21 (26 days) added 3; Sep 5 -> Sep 21 (16 days) added 2.
- Conditional on July only: 31-32 cumulative at month boundaries, ~8 new in the month (~2.6/10 days).
- Zero 10-day window since Aug 1 has added more than about 2 cases; no window since June has added more than 3.
- Case-to-premises ratio in Texas (50 animal cases vs 39 premises) implies occasional multi-animal confirmations from a single site, i.e. counts arrive in small clumps rather than strictly one at a time.

MARKETS: Kalshi lists series KXSCREWWORMCOUNT with 2026 calendar thresholds at 0/1/2/3/5/10 cases closing 2027-01-01 - thresholds, deadline and resolution source (CDC/WHO/national health agencies) all differ from this question, and the quoted last prices are stale/inconsistent with 50 confirmed cases. calls.reasoning: Monotonic count, currently 50 (APHIS via trackers, 2026-09-21 14:05 CT), so the question is purely how many confirmations land in the ~10 remaining days. Reference class is 10-day increments of this same series: ~0.12 cases/day over Aug 26-Sep 21 (3 cases) and 4 cases in all of August, implying a Poisson mean near 1.2 additions, so 50 or 51 is the modal landing zone. I widened the right tail for two reasons: confirmations arrive in clusters (a single infested premises can yield several animals at once, as in June's 9-in-8-days run), and the surveillance story is contested - officials call the decline biologically implausible and suspect under-reporting, so a detection push or a first wildlife case could dump a backlog. Counterweight: sterile-fly releases are scaling, northward spread has reportedly slowed, and Texas is releasing quarantine zones (Edwards, Sutton, Val Verde, Uvalde EDOs dated Sep 21), all consistent with continued suppression. Thin-evidence caveat: the APHIS dashboard is not text-scrapeable and no market prices this, so I lean close to the recent-pace base rate.

calls.reasoning: The count is monotonic and stood at 50 on 2026-09-21, so this is purely about confirmations posting in the remaining ~9.7 days. The post-peak regime runs ~0.115 cases/day (3 additions Aug 26 -> Sep 21; 4 in all of August vs ~30 in June), implying ~1.1 additions before Oct 1 - so 50 and 51 are the modal landings and 52 is the 75th percentile. Suppression signals are concrete and current: TAHC released or modified infested zones in 13+ counties through Sep 21 (Edwards, Sutton, Val Verde, Uvalde EDOs dated that day), sterile-fly releases at ~1bn males, federal officials reporting northward spread slowed. Upside mechanisms exist but lack a trigger inside the window: multi-animal premises clusters (50 cases across 39 TX premises), NM's expanded surveillance from Sep 20, the September border reopening to Mexican livestock, and credible expert scepticism that the decline is biologically real - but suspected under-reporting inflates true incidence, not the reported dashboard figure, and hunter-season wildlife surveillance opens after Oct 1. No market prices this contract: Kalshi's KXSCREWWORMCOUNT uses different thresholds, a 2027-01-01 close and CDC/WHO resolution; Manifold's wild-animal contract (0.79, vol 1,722, closes 2026-12-31) is a different event on a different deadline - evidence, not an anchor, and not blended.
calls.reconciliation: The three runs are near-identical on evidence and differ mainly on right-tail width (Run 1: 90th at 54.3, dispersion 4.4; Runs 2/3: 90th at 53.5, dispersion ~3.4). I side with the narrower reading because the series contains no post-Aug-1 10-day window above +2 and no scheduled event inside the window that would trigger a backlog dump, while still carrying enough mass at 53-54 for a premises cluster. Factual check on the starting level: all three independently land on 50 (48 TX + 2 NM) from separate restatements of APHIS, so I adopt it - but none read the APHIS dashboard itself (Power BI embed; genomicepi/dvm360 403), so a Sep 18-21 confirmation not picked up by news could mean the dashboard already reads 51. That unresolvable ambiguity is strictly upward, which is part of why my median sits at 51 rather than on the 50 status-quo atom. Run-level disagreement about July's total (11 vs 13) does not move the estimate: all three compute the operative rate from Aug 26 -> Sep 21. Dashboard posting lag (detections after ~Sep 28 may not appear) is real but roughly neutral in a steady-state pipeline, since lagged earlier detections post inside the window too; I did not shrink the mean for it. No web access this run - settled entirely on the dossiers.
